# Engine changelog

Every engine version, what it changed, and whether results stay comparable across it. Authored once in `scsim/CHANGELOG.yaml` and gated in CI (PLAN.md §25, gate `engine-ledger`). *Comparable* answers the user's question; *Tier* is the engineering classification (Part IX §9.5) — a patch can still change results for some projects.

## 0.8.3 · 2026-10-27 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for a scenario that ticks Safety stock and sets a buffer window; every other scenario runs exactly as before (every frozen reference run kept its digest).

Safety stock is now a real recovery strategy. For the materials a disrupted supplier ships, a scenario can hold extra days of cover between a start week and an end week: the reorder levels rise only in those weeks, so the buffer is built from orders placed at the start and arrives a lead time later, and its holding cost is charged at the material's own holding rate for those weeks only. The /policies safety stock is unchanged, and a scenario that sets no buffer runs exactly as before.

*Technical.* P-P.3 `windows` (`SafetyStockWindow`: material_id, days, start_week, end_week exclusive): E[D_m]·days/7 added to s and S at PH-70 while active (never to a stated level); holding h_m·c_m·units booked in `ss_holding` for active weeks. The mapper maps `recovery.safety_stock_windows` under the `safety_stock_drawdown` response (and only while recovery is enabled), skips a malformed window with its reason, and warns for a material the project does not simulate, for an MRP inventory policy (which reads no reorder levels), and for Safety stock ticked with no window. `engineBridge.json` maps the response to `safety_stock_materials`; the pre-run grader honours `enabled: false`.

- commit: not yet recorded
- policies P-P.3
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D315

**Changed under this version without a bump:**

- 2026-11-07 · Tier 1 — Decision traces, first slice (policy facet 11; platform blueprint §6.1, ai-agents.md §5.5). A single-replication inspection run (`trace_verbosity=full_debug`, one replication) now carries `ScenarioResult.decision_trace`: one record per policy decision with its week, policy, material, the rationale code that decided, the values the rule read and what it did. P-S.1 (backup supplier) is the first policy that records, including why it did NOT reroute. Each policy declares its rationale codes (`rationale_codes`), which the registry export publishes. Recording only reads values the policy already computed, so no KPI, series or frozen reference run moved, and an ordinary Monte Carlo run is unchanged.

## 0.8.2 · 2026-10-27 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for a scenario whose playbook switches recovery off while ticking strategies, states a strategy cost or horizon, or enters a backup supplier; every other scenario runs exactly as before (every frozen reference run kept its digest).

A scenario's recovery playbook now runs as it reads. "Recovery enabled" off switches every recovery strategy off (it was never read, so ticked strategies ran anyway). Each strategy's cost or horizon field reaches its policy instead of being ignored, and the backup lead time can be left blank to mean each backup supplier's own. A backup supplier can be entered on a scenario for a material no uploaded supplier backs up: it is used only while the primary is disrupted and is never made the primary. A strategy the engine does not model is named in the run's notes instead of being silently dropped.

*Technical.* `recovery_responses()` gates `_map_policies` on `recovery.enabled`. `backup_lead_time_weeks` → P-S.1 `backup_lead_time_weeks` (blank = the link's own), `overtime_cost_pct` → P-P.5 `overtime_premium_pct_of_price`, `expedite_cost_pct` → P-T.2 `premium_pct_of_cost`, `allocation_horizon_weeks` / `annual_labor_cost` → P-P.9 `window_weeks` / `annual_cost`. `SupplierLink.backup_only` (default false): `primary_rank` ranks it after every uploaded link, `CompiledModel.link_backup_only` excludes it from P-S.2's planned shares, and `_scenario_backup_links` adds one per `recovery.backup_lanes` entry only while `dual_source_activate` is on, with a `Supplier` for an id no uploaded lane names. A `safety_stock_drawdown` or `demand_shaping` response earns a mapping warning.

- commit: not yet recorded
- policies P-S.1, P-S.2, P-P.5, P-P.9, P-T.2
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D114, D315

## 0.8.1 · 2026-10-21 · Tier 2

**Comparable — results unchanged.** No existing scenario can carry a material event, so every result is unchanged (every frozen reference run kept its digest); material outages are new.

A single material can now be disrupted: every supplier's deliveries of that material stop for the outage, and nothing else those suppliers ship is affected. Backup-supplier, multi-sourcing, expediting and material-allocation policies see the outage per material, so a supplier's healthy materials are never treated as disrupted. Every existing scenario runs exactly as before.

*Technical.* `TargetType.NODE_MATERIAL` (lead_time_extension only; a capacity cut stays per supplier). `ResolvedEvent.material_idx`; `SimContext.link_lt_block_end` (per link) composed with the per-supplier block by the later end in the week_start mechanic, the arrival deferral and the quoted arrival. `SimContext.visible_disrupted_links()` is read by P-S.1, P-S.2, P-T.2 and P-P.9 in place of the supplier mask indexed by link. The project mapper and the platform's dispatch gate are unchanged: a `material:*` schedule entry is still skipped there (§4 D112).

- commit: not yet recorded
- policies P-S.1, P-S.2, P-T.2, P-P.9
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D311, WP 17.1

**Changed under this version without a bump:**

- 2026-10-21 · Tier 2 — The nexus battery (`scsim.stress.nexus`, PLAN.md §27 WP 17.2): every supplier and every supplied material disrupted alone under one shared scenario — a full outage from week 26, or the first week after warm-up if later, for each of 2–9 weeks — with the lost sales in € paired against the undisrupted run, ranked by the average over the eight durations. The scenario is exported to the registry as `nexus_scenario`. A new library entry point only: no existing run, KPI or frozen reference run moved.
- 2026-10-27 · Tier 2 — The nexus battery can run a declared variant of its shared scenario — another start week and/or another set of outage durations (`nexus_variant`), owner-requested for one 5-week outage from week 30 — stored whole beside its own hash; and a stored battery now records the root seed it ran on. The shared scenario and every result of it are unchanged: no existing run, KPI or frozen reference run moved.

## 0.8.0 · 2026-10-04 · Tier 3

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for projects whose products carry a production lead time (L > 0) or its shape; L = 0, the default, runs byte-identically (every frozen reference run kept its digest).

A product can take time to make: a production lead time per product, fixed or drawn from a distribution like a supplier's, so what starts this week is finished stock some weeks later. Planned production is offset by the expected lead time and work in progress is traced. A product with no production lead time completes in the week it starts, as before.

*Technical.* P-P.13 (new): a per-product production pipeline ring — `production_started` is what starts at t, `production_output` what completes (t − L); a new world spawn key draws each product's lead time (`seeds.product_prodtime_rng`), with the shapes of `core/leadtime.py`; the plan reads `production_lead_time_offset` (E[L]). Mapper keys `prod_lead_time_*`. Pipeline schema stamp only.

- commit: not yet recorded
- ADR 0003
- policies P-P.13
- KPIs `fill_rate`, `lost_sales_value`
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D300, D301, WP 16.4, WP 16.5, ADR 0003

**Changed under this version without a bump:**

- 2026-10-20 · Tier 2 — An inspection run (one replication, full trace) also records each product's finished-goods stock and its target week by week (`product.fg_on_hand`, `product.fg_target`, summing to `fg_units`) and the fulfillment mode the engine resolved (`product.make_to_stock`, 1 = make-to-stock). Output only: no KPI, series or frozen reference run moved.

## 0.7.0 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 3

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for projects whose lanes or materials select normal, triangular or uniform lead times; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

A supplier lead time can follow a normal, triangular or uniform distribution, chosen per supplier × material row with only the parameters that shape needs, as demand is. A bounded shape plans on the mean of its bounds. Lognormal and gamma lead times and every project with no new shape are unchanged.

*Technical.* P-S.6 widened: `LeadTimeDist` gains normal / triangular / uniform; their standard uniforms are drawn per (lane, week) from a new world spawn key (`seeds.lane_leadtime_rng`, one child stream per lane) before any policy acts, and turned into a lead time by the one inverse CDF in `core/leadtime.py`. A bounded link's planning lead time is its bounds' mean; P-P.3's King formula reads the shape's own σ/μ. Pipeline schema stamp only.

- ADR 0003

## 0.6.1 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for projects whose Supplier rows carry a typed s or S, a periodic review period, or an (R,Q) lot; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

A replenishment level typed on a /policies Supplier row is now exactly the level the run uses: no safety stock is added on top of it and it is never raised. Periodic review reads its review period per material, and an (R,Q) policy with a lot size orders up to R + Q.

*Technical.* P-P.1/P-P.3: a row's absolute s/S is the material's level (P-P.3 adds nothing on top at PH-70); periodic T read per material; (R,Q) with a lot has S = R + Q; Eq. 21 reads the row κ. Patch: no new phase or state key. Mapping warning text for `order_up_to` reworded.

## 0.2.7 · 2026-09-22 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results can change for runs with automatic warm-up, where the adopted warm-up week moves; rare and small in the reference set.

Automatic warm-up detection uses the published MSER-5 statistic (White, 1997).

*Technical.* mser5 is z(d) = Σ(b−b̄)²/(n_b−d)². The old statistic is reported for one release as `WarmupReport.mser5_legacy_week` and adopted by nothing. Of 36 auto-warm-up reference scenarios the adopted warm-up changed in 1 (week 50 → 60); its fill rate moved +0.0003, inside its CI.
